name: Dr. Rubeena Kidwai
idea_context: An estimated 1 in 8 Pakistanis experience psychological distress, yet most never seek care: stigma, poor access, high out-of-pocket costs, and roughly one mental-health professional per 500,000 people. Untreated mental illness costs Pakistan about $4B a year in lost productivity.
mission: Accessible, affordable, stigma-free mental health care for every Pakistani.
how_it_works: A helpline coordinator, supported by an AI-powered WhatsApp bot and IVR, triages every caller. Urgent cases are flagged; others are booked into a structured 40-minute consultation with a licensed psychologist, with referrals to psychiatrists where needed, delivered through a virtual infrastructure of multilingual clinicians working remotely across Pakistan.
the_dream: A government-run national mental health helpline, powered by Taskeen's design, systems and training, serving millions. Doer and payer at scale: government.
card_summary: Coordinators triage every caller with AI support; a licensed psychologist takes a structured 40-minute consultation.

scale.good: 70% of people supported show clinically meaningful improvement on PHQ-9 and GAD-7; 89% satisfaction; $117 per YLD averted.
scale.big: A 1-in-8 prevalence in a country of 250M, and a phone line reaches wherever there is a signal.
scale.simple: Centralized triage plus remote multilingual clinicians; an AI WhatsApp chatbot (Taskeen Dost) is next, to extend lay counselling and strengthen triage.
scale.cheap: $23 per patient today, targeting under $15 at scale.

so_far: 25,000+ people supported via the helpline (Sept 2020 to June 2026)
70% demonstrated clinically meaningful improvement; 89% satisfied
Helped decriminalise suicide in Pakistan

name: Azima Dhanjee
idea_context: There are 70M Deaf individuals globally and 5M in Pakistan alone; over 80% cannot read and rely on sign language as their primary mode of communication. Pakistan would need 13,000 interpreters to serve its Deaf population, and interpretation is needed everywhere: health, finance, education, employment.
mission: Enable Deaf people to live independently.
how_it_works: A Deaf user downloads the ConnectHear app with SILA, its sign-language AI agent. A hearing person speaks or types and SILA converts it into sign language; the Deaf user signs and SILA converts it into text and audio. Professionally trained Deaf interpreters and native signers label, validate and continuously expand the signing dataset SILA is trained on.
the_dream: Sign language as the third language of the internet. Doer at scale: other businesses. Payer at scale: customers, individuals and government.
card_summary: A hearing person speaks into the app; SILA, their sign-language AI, signs back. A Deaf user signs, and SILA turns it into voice and text.

scale.good: 50,000 registered users, 3,000 calls a month, and 200 Deaf people employed through the platform. The impact metric they hold themselves to is independence: the share of Deaf users still active at three months who report feeling more independent.
scale.big: 5M Deaf people in Pakistan and 70M worldwide, with interpretation needed across health, finance, education and employment.
scale.simple: The app is the delivery vehicle; the hard, defensible part, a 250,000+ word Indo-Pak Sign Language dataset, is already built and compounds with use. Real-time sign-to-text remains the technical frontier.
scale.cheap: About $3 per user per month today at 3,000 users (human interpretation, B2B-subsidized); target of $0.03 per user per month at 750,000+ users once SILA's AI interpretation scales.

so_far: 50,000 registered users and 3,000 monthly calls (end 2025)
200 Deaf people employed through the platform
250,000+ word Indo-Pak Sign Language database, plus an AI content tool for disaster notifications

name: Habiba Banu
idea_context: A child living with someone who has TB has roughly a 1-in-15 chance of developing TB. Prevention is simple and effective, yet only about 4 of every 100 children who need preventive treatment receive it; the route to it is a facility visit that costs a family lost wages and a long clinic trip.
how_it_works: Every adult TB diagnosis tells the health system which children are at risk and where they live. Field staff get the patient's details from the public TB clinic, call the family, and visit the home: 1 visit, 4 symptoms checked for every household member, and 12 weekly doses of preventive medicine prescribed on the spot via telemedicine for symptom-free under-5s, with follow-up to completion.
the_dream: TB prevention reaches every at-risk child in Pakistan as a routine, government-run part of the health system; at national scale about 5,500 TB cases prevented and 450 lives saved each year. Doer and payer at scale: government.
card_summary: Every adult diagnosis points to exposed children. Staff visit the home, screen everyone, and start preventive treatment there.

scale.good: 80% preventive-medicine coverage where Spiro works, against a roughly 4% national baseline, with a modelled 70% reduction in TB cases among those covered.
scale.big: A national problem with a mapped delivery route: every diagnosis in the public system points to the next household.
scale.simple: A 1-visit, 4-symptom, 12-dose protocol run by field staff plus a doctor on the phone; now being handed to government-funded community health workers in Punjab.
scale.cheap: $20 per person given preventive medicine; $550 per TB case prevented.

so_far: 5,800 people reached with preventive medicine, 2,900 of them under 5 (June 2026)
Working with 22 hospitals across 7 districts of Sindh
Expanding to all 30 Sindh districts by November 2026, plus a Punjab launch with government community health inspectors

name: Lala Rukh Fazal-Ur-Rahman
tagline: Simple, effective science lessons integrated into the curriculum
idea_context: Beyond Pakistan's 26 million out-of-school children, science for those in school is dominated by rote memorization. Girls and children from low-income communities in particular build low science capital: the knowledge, experiences and confidence to see science as theirs.
how_it_works: Sustained teacher training plus a continuous supply of bite-sized, curriculum-aligned inquiry activities in local languages, built from low-cost, locally available materials. Teachers experience the science themselves in training, then get a year of follow-up support until inquiry becomes their normal way of teaching, inside the existing timetable.
the_dream: Inquiry-based science as a normal part of primary education across public and low-cost private schools. Doer at scale: government systems and school networks. Payer at scale: education budgets, with development partners supporting adoption during scale-up.
card_summary: Teachers get sustained training and a stream of bite-sized experiments built from cheap local materials.

scale.good: Tracks conceptual understanding and scientific reasoning pre/post, plus confidence and belonging; commissioning rigorous independent evidence is their stated top priority.
scale.big: Millions of primary students across public and low-cost private school networks.
scale.simple: No specialist equipment, no new infrastructure, no extra class time: a weekly hands-on inquiry session inside the existing timetable.
scale.cheap: About $7 per child per year today; $3 to $5 target at scale through standardized content and WhatsApp-based teacher support.

so_far: 98,000 children reached through hands-on science programmes (2019 to 2026)
1,800 teachers trained and supported
50 schools using the tools within regular teaching

name: Khushbakht Shah Jillani
tagline: A DIY divorce tool for women in abusive marriages
idea_context: One in three married women in Pakistan experiences intimate-partner violence, which is more than 20 million women. The law gives them the right to leave, but using that right means hiring a lawyer, and most women cannot afford one, safely reach one, or trust one. Many stay in dangerous marriages simply because the exit is out of reach.
mission: Make the legal exit from an abusive marriage fast, affordable, and simple enough that any woman can complete it.
how_it_works: Khushbakht has spent eight years litigating family-law cases, more than 160 of them, and Mehfooz builds that courtroom experience into an AI assistant. A woman starts with a chatbot, which first checks whether she is in danger. The free tier prepares her complete, court-ready divorce file. The paid Court Companion (PKR 3,500, about $12.60) then walks her through the affidavits, documents and self-representation steps up to filing, and certified lawyers review the difficult calls before anything is filed.
the_dream: Every completed case pays for itself and funds the next one, so leaving safely becomes infrastructure rather than charity. At scale the woman herself does the work, with AI as her tool, and the bill is paid by her, by a sponsor, or by an institution.
card_summary: A chatbot checks her safety first, then prepares her complete court-ready divorce file. Certified lawyers review it before filing.

scale.good: Khushbakht is one of Pakistan's most sought-after divorce lawyers, and her 160+ litigated cases are what the product is trained on. Independent research supports the approach: a 2026 randomised trial involving 1,559 judges (Mehmood, Goessmann & Ash) found that expert-trained legal AI improves case outcomes. Evidence from Mehfooz's own cases is now being gathered through the live pilot.
scale.big: More than 20 million affected women in Pakistan, and khula is a clear legal right once a case is properly filed.
scale.simple: The AI handles the volume and a network of certified lawyers handles the judgment, so the service scales without the founder in the loop. It spreads through women-only community networks, which costs almost nothing.
scale.cheap: The woman herself pays PKR 3,500 (about $12.60), so every case funds the service. The company is bootstrapped and was earning revenue before taking any outside money.

so_far: A live pilot with 20 women in Sindh is already generating revenue
The team has grown from 5 to 19 people since July 2026, and Maleeka Bokhari, who wrote Pakistan's Anti-Rape Act 2021, has joined the board
By November 30 they aim to reach 100,000 paid Members Room subscribers (PKR 999 per month)

name: Maira Siddiqui
tagline: Tools for native-language instruction in elementary schools
idea_context: Of the 70 million children enrolled in Pakistani schools, 77% cannot read or write basic age-appropriate text, because they are expected to decode a foreign language, English, before they can grasp basic literacy.
mission: Educate all Pakistani children using their native language.
how_it_works: Chiragh Taleem, a K-5 Urdu literacy app, supercharged with Bubbly, an offline-first conversational voice AI that speaks regional languages such as Pashto, Punjabi and Sindhi. A child chooses their language by voice and learns National Curriculum Urdu and math completely text-free, with offline progress tracking synced to school dashboards and EGRA/EGMA-benchmarked evaluation run with partner TTWF.
the_dream: Become the onebillion of Pakistan: foundational literacy for 26M out-of-school children and reading fluency for 46M enrolled students. Doer and payer at scale: initially Chiragh with NGOs and INGOs, eventually the Government of Pakistan.
card_summary: Bubbly, an offline voice tutor, speaks Pashto, Punjabi and Sindhi, so a child who cannot read yet can learn Urdu and math.

scale.good: EGRA/EGMA pre-, mid- and endline testing with TTWF; the metric is non-literate children reaching fluent Grade-1 mother-tongue reading within a 6-month window.
scale.big: 26M out-of-school children plus 46M enrolled students, across six-plus regional languages.
scale.simple: Ships on a USB drive and runs offline on tablets; partner organizations' facilitators are trained to run it in their classrooms.
scale.cheap: $6 per child per year for the app license today, targeting $5, or $50 per child per year including a solar-charged tablet amortized over three years.

so_far: A contracted institutional pipeline of 60,000+ out-of-school children with TTWF and the Sindh Education Foundation
140,000 organic YouTube subscribers on Chiragh Kids TV, 10,000+ monthly returning viewers
$80,000 in early field-testing revenue over three years

name: Adnan Qureshi
tagline: Full tablet learning for left-out kids
idea_context: Over 26 million children are out of school in Pakistan, and many who are enrolled fail to reach foundational learning; only 50 to 60% of 5th graders perform at 2nd-grade level.
mission: Make kids grade-level literate by making schools accessible to all.
how_it_works: One-room, solar-powered Digital MicroSchools: low-cost Android tablets running offline, gamified adaptive learning software for English, Math and local language, run by locally hired women facilitators, with ongoing community mobilization and governance dashboards.
the_dream: Universal foundational literacy; learning poverty in Pakistan down from 78% to single digits; global replication of the Digital MicroSchool model. Doer and payer at scale: government.
card_summary: Solar-powered classrooms, adaptive learning games, and locally hired women facilitators bring school to villages that have none.

scale.good: 6,500+ out-of-school children mainstreamed into formal or vocational pathways; the core metric is % improvement in K-5 learning outcomes.
scale.big: 26M out-of-school children in Pakistan alone, with deployments already in Pakistan, Bangladesh, Malawi and South Sudan.
scale.simple: An offline-first kit: a room, tablets, software and a locally hired facilitator, designed for low-connectivity places. A franchise playbook to let others replicate it is the next build.
scale.cheap: $132 per student per year at current scale, heading below $100 by early 2027.

so_far: 47,000+ out-of-school children reached since 2021
25,000+ children actively enrolled across 264 deployments (July 2026)
Sindh government Phase 3 scaling plan: 300 more MicroSchools in 2027 and 300 in 2028

name: Muhammad Waqas
tagline: Low-cost video games to boost disabled kids' abilities
idea_context: 240 million children live with a disability and are 49% more likely to never attend school. Therapy and special education cost $10,000 to $60,000 per child per year, and in most of the world the specialists simply do not exist; Pakistan has roughly one therapist for every 230,000 people.
mission: Give every child with special needs a fighting chance to learn, grow and develop.
how_it_works: Clinically designed therapy and special-education exercises become augmented-reality movement games. A child stands in front of any laptop, tablet or phone, sees themselves on screen, and plays; the AI reads their body movement through the ordinary camera. No sensors, no clinic. Every game is built with therapists, psychologists and special educators, and progress reports generate automatically for parents, teachers and government dashboards.
the_dream: Every child with special needs, anywhere, gets access to therapy through play. Doer at scale: WonderTree as a platform. Payer at scale: schools, therapy centers, governments and families, through subscriptions.
card_summary: A child plays clinically designed exercises as AR games on any phone or laptop; progress reports write themselves.

scale.good: Two published randomised controlled trials (Games for Health Journal; Frontiers in Neurology, which recorded a 13% improvement in balance and a Cohen’s d of 1.9 on upper-extremity function). In the Zayed Higher Organization deployment across 9 Abu Dhabi centers, 80% of 324 children improved in at least one tracked skill.
scale.big: 240M children with disabilities globally; it works wherever there is a phone or laptop with a camera. Live in English and Arabic, with Greek and Urdu coming.
scale.simple: Runs in a browser on any device with a camera, and any adult can facilitate with almost no training, which is what makes it work where there is no therapist at all.
scale.cheap: Around 80% cheaper than conventional therapy, priced market by market. Profitable in FY2025 at close to a 20% net margin on about $166,000 in revenue.

so_far: 17,177 children reached across 200+ institutions in Pakistan, the UAE and the US
92% of teachers report visible improvement; in rural Sindh, half saw change within 4 to 8 sessions
Backed by UNICEF, UNDP, the GSMA Innovation Fund, the LEGO Foundation, the Google SDG Accelerator and MIT Solve; US patent under review

name: Ali Siddiq
tagline: Skills training for the modern economy
idea_context: 64% of Pakistan's roughly 250M people are under 30, yet youth unemployment among degree holders exceeds 30% and is rising. Employers consistently report that graduates lack workplace skills: communication, problem-solving, initiative, adaptability.
mission: Get underserved Pakistani university students into meaningful work.
how_it_works: A three-month experiential career-prep fellowship: repeated, scaffolded practice of real professional behaviors with structured reflection and feedback in a supportive peer cohort. Now being embedded as a for-credit course in public-sector universities, delivered by university faculty whom Amal selects, trains and coaches.
the_dream: Seven years: embedded in all public-sector universities in Pakistan. Fifteen years: university-embedded career prep scaling in dozens of countries. Doer and payer at scale: government, through existing university budgets.
card_summary: Students get three months of real workplace practice, embedded in public universities and taught by faculty Amal trains.

scale.good: 81% of job-seeking Fellows start work within three months of the program, with 1.5 to 2x improvements in key skills and mindsets.
scale.big: Every public-university graduate in Pakistan; the model has run continuously since 2014.
scale.simple: University faculty deliver it themselves after Amal's training and coaching, so the organization does not have to grow with every new cohort.
scale.cheap: $300 fully loaded per Fellow today in direct delivery; $75 at scale, most of it absorbed by existing university staff budgets.

so_far: 16,000 Fellows graduated (2014 to 2026)
First university-led, for-credit pilot launches Fall 2026
2 to 3 additional universities being lined up for an expanded 2027 pilot

name: Osama Shahid
tagline: A one-stop shop for high-productivity ag products
idea_context: Nearly 80% of Pakistani farmers cultivate less than five acres and suffer the lowest farm productivity in the region, driven by lack of access to affordable tools and practical knowledge.
mission: Double the income of Pakistani smallholder farmers and serve a million farmers by 2035.
how_it_works: Sources proven small-scale machines from global manufacturers and re-engineers them for Pakistani crops, soils and repair conditions. Field demonstrations teach the economics of ownership; four 3S stores (sales, service, spares), a website and a contact centre sell farmer-direct with no dealer layers. Train-the-trainer programs build local operator networks, and a multilingual WhatsApp mechanic is being built to handle diagnosis and repair anywhere.
the_dream: Every small farm in Pakistan runs on machines, not muscle. Doer at scale: Soby, a profitable direct-to-farmer business, plus the private sector that follows. Payer at scale: the farmers themselves; machines recover their cost within 3 to 12 months.
card_summary: Soby adapts proven small machines to Pakistani crops, sells them farmer-direct, and teaches farmers to run them profitably.

scale.good: 11,271 customers adopting mechanization with increased productivity and income; every product is field-tested until it works, and breaks, predictably.
scale.big: Roughly 80% of Pakistan's farms are smallholdings, and the model needs no subsidy to spread.
scale.simple: A store, a field demo, a trained local operator network, and soon a WhatsApp mechanic in Urdu, Punjabi, Sindhi, Pashto and Balochi.
scale.cheap: The farmer pays because the machine returns its cost in 3 to 12 months; the top-selling harvester costs one-fifth of a tractor setup. Cost per beneficiary: $65.5 (FY2025).

so_far: 11,271 cumulative customers served through mechanization
67,626 cumulative beneficiaries (average household of six)
22,542 cumulative rural jobs created (through FY2026)
